What is EigenLayer?

EigenLayer is a middleware protocol built on Ethereum that introduces restaking — a groundbreaking mechanism that allows ETH stakers to reuse their staked ETH to secure additional networks and protocols, called Actively Validated Services (AVSs), without any additional capital outlay. In essence, your staked ETH becomes the security backbone for an entire ecosystem of decentralized services.

When you stake ETH natively on Ethereum or deposit Lido stETH or Rocket Pool rETH into EigenLayer, you opt into securing AVSs. In return, you earn additional restaking rewards on top of your existing staking yield. This creates a "security as a service" marketplace where AVS teams can rent security from ETH stakers rather than spending years bootstrapping their own validator networks — a process that would cost millions and take significant time.

The genius of restaking lies in its permissionless, shared security model. Unlike traditional validator businesses that operate in silos, restakers contribute to a pooled security primitive. An AVS like a data availability layer, a cross-chain bridge, an oracle network, or a rollup sequencer can plug into this pool and benefit from Ethereum's massive ETH security overnight. For stakers, this means your ETH works harder — earning yields from multiple sources simultaneously.

Every restaker runs an EigenPod — a smart contract on Ethereum that monitors and proves validator behavior. If an operator assigned to your delegated stake misbehaves or an AVS you support experiences a slashing event, a portion of your restaked ETH can be "slashed" as a penalty. This is the critical tradeoff: higher yield comes with higher risk, because you're now exposed to slashing from multiple AVSs, not just Ethereum consensus.

EigenLayer's architecture separates concerns into three roles: stakers (ETH holders who deposit and delegate), operators (entities that run the infrastructure for AVSs), and AVS developers (teams building services that need decentralized security). Stakers can choose to directly operate nodes or delegate to professional operators. The protocol supports both native restaking (for node operators) and liquid restaking (depositing LSTs like stETH/rETH), making restaking accessible to anyone with ETH.

The EigenLayer governance token (EIGEN) was introduced to align incentives between the protocol and restakers. EIGEN serves as a "slashing担保" — when insufficient ETH is available to cover slashing penalties, EIGEN tokens can be auctioned to replenish the slashing pool. This creates a secondary layer of security beyond pure ETH collateral.

With over $14.8 billion in TVL and growing, EigenLayer has become one of the most influential DeFi primitives since its mainnet launch. It powers security for protocols including EigenDA (data availability), Hyperlane (bridging), Celo's Mento oracles, and many more. The restaking model is reshaping how decentralized networks acquire security — turning Ethereum's staked capital into a programmable, composable security layer for the entire crypto ecosystem.

Risk Considerations

⚠️

Slashing Risk

Unlike simple ETH staking, restaking exposes your collateral to slashing events from multiple AVSs simultaneously. If an AVS experiences a consensus failure or oracle manipulation, operators and their delegators can be slashed. Use the simulator above to stress-test your positions and always maintain a buffer.

LowMediumHigh
🔐

Smart Contract Risk

EigenLayer's contracts are relatively new compared to battle-tested protocols like Aave. The upgradeable proxy pattern used by EigenLayer contracts carries risk of governance attacks or upgrade key compromise. Audits reduce but don't eliminate this risk. The EIGEN token adds an additional smart contract attack surface.

LowMediumHigh
👥

Operator Risk

When you delegate to an operator, you're trusting them to run honest, performant infrastructure. A incompetent or malicious operator can trigger slashing events that affect all their delegators. Research operator history, uptime, and slashing track record before delegating — and spread delegation across multiple operators.

LowMediumHigh
📉

TVL & Correlation Risk

When a significant portion of ETH is restaked through EigenLayer, a mass slashing event could trigger cascading liquidations and network instability. Additionally, restaked assets have a shared risk correlation — one AVS hack could trigger slashing across many restakers simultaneously, unlike isolated DeFi positions.

LowMediumHigh

Glossary of Terms

Restaking
Reusing staked ETH to secure additional networks (AVSs) without additional capital. You continue earning Ethereum staking rewards while also earning AVS validation rewards.
AVS (Actively Validated Service)
Any decentralized service that needs its own consensus or validation layer — oracles, bridges, data availability layers, rollup provers, etc. AVSs plug into EigenLayer's shared security pool.
EigenPod
A smart contract on Ethereum that serves as proof-of-stake validator for restaking. When you restake natively, you deploy an EigenPod that monitors your validator's behavior and handles slashing proofs.
Slashing
A penalty mechanism where a portion of a validator's or restaker's staked ETH is destroyed for equivocation, downtime, or AVS validation failures. Unlike simple staking slashing, restaking multiplies exposure to slashing events.
Delegation
When restakers don't want to run their own nodes, they delegate their stake to professional operators who run the AVS infrastructure on their behalf. Operators charge a commission fee on earned rewards.
Operator
An entity that runs the technical infrastructure (nodes, validators) required to secure AVSs. Operators accept delegations from restakers and earn a commission on the rewards generated.
Native Restaking
Directly staking ETH by running an Ethereum validator and registering an EigenPod. Requires 32 ETH minimum and node operation expertise. Offers the highest level of decentralization.
Liquid Restaking
Depositing liquid staking tokens (LSTs) like stETH or rETH into EigenLayer to earn restaking rewards. More accessible than native restaking — anyone with LSTs can participate without running a node.
EIGEN Token
The governance and slashing insurance token of EigenLayer. Used as secondary collateral when ETH is insufficient to cover slashing events. EIGEN holders participate in protocol governance decisions.
Slashing Attack Surface
The total amount of ETH exposed to potential slashing across all AVSs you're supporting. More AVSs supported = higher attack surface = higher potential loss from slashing events.
